title: Jupiter and the Monkey
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Jupiter issued a proclamation to all the beasts, and offered a prize to the one who, in his judgment, produced the most beautiful offspring. Among the rest came the Monkey, carrying a baby monkey in her arms, a hairless, flat-nosed little fright. When they saw it, the gods all burst into peal on peal of laughter; but the Monkey hugged her little one to her, and said, "Jupiter may give the prize to whomsoever he likes: but I shall always think my baby the most beautiful of them all."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Jupiter offer to the beast who produced the most beautiful offspring?
options: A place at his own table
A prize
A new home in the forest
A crown of laurels

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Monkey carry in her arms?
options: A bundle of straw
A piece of fruit
A baby monkey
A small mirror

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how is the baby monkey described?
options: As a hairless, flat-nosed little fright
As a plump and cheerful little creature
As the largest baby among the beasts
As quiet and unusually well-behaved

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the gods react when they saw the baby monkey?
options: They turned away in disgust
They demanded Jupiter disqualify the Monkey
They burst into peal on peal of laughter
They fell completely silent

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Monkey do while the gods laughed?
options: She hid her baby behind her back
She laughed along with the gods
She left the gathering in anger
She hugged her little one to her

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Monkey say she will always think about her baby?
options: That he will grow up to be strong
That he is the most beautiful of them all
That he deserves Jupiter's prize regardless
That he will one day rule the beasts

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Monkey say Jupiter may give the prize to whomsoever he likes?
options: She has already decided her baby has no chance of winning fairly
Her own opinion of her baby's beauty does not depend on Jupiter's judgment or anyone else's laughter
She wants to flatter Jupiter into changing his mind
She believes the contest itself is meaningless

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A parent's love makes her own child seem beautiful, however others see it
Jupiter's contests always favor the largest beasts
Beasts should never enter contests judged by the gods
Laughter from others always changes a mother's opinion of her child

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Jupiter issue to all the beasts?
options: A challenge to a race
A proclamation
A warning
An invitation to a feast

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whose judgment was to decide which offspring was most beautiful?
options: The Monkey's
The other beasts' combined vote
Jupiter's own judgment
A panel of gods chosen at random

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Monkey say Jupiter may do with the prize?
options: Keep it for himself
Give it to whomsoever he likes
Divide it among all the beasts
Save it for next year's contest

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what makes the gods' laughter and the Monkey's response form a contrast?
options: The gods laugh at the baby's looks while the Monkey still calls him the most beautiful
The gods laugh with joy while the Monkey weeps with shame
The gods praise the baby while the Monkey criticizes him
The gods ignore the baby while the Monkey demands attention for him

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fright" mean in "a hairless, flat-nosed little fright"?
options: A sudden feeling of fear
An odd-looking, unattractive creature
A loud, startling noise
A fast-moving animal

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Monkey wins Jupiter's beauty contest outright
Jupiter disqualifies the Monkey's baby from the contest
The gods laugh at the Monkey's odd-looking baby, but she declares him the most beautiful regardless
The Monkey refuses to enter her baby in the contest at all
